digest.component_or_area: inbound reconciler parent-field diffing and peer-evidence gating
propositions: When a Jira parent is removed (set to None), the local parent_id is not cleared because the snapshot omits absent parents and the differ refuses None emissions without peer evidence.

The fetcher and differ form two independent layers that each suppress the parent-clear signal: layer 1 leaves the parent field absent in the snapshot, and layer 2 refuses to emit parent_id=None without positive proof the peer once carried the parent.

A clear must fire only on positive evidence that the peer once had the parent, tracked in the binding store as per-binding state and advanced by reconcile only when the parent key is observed in the snapshot.

The managed_refs gate alone cannot decide whether to clear because it only proves the ref was set locally, never whether the peer ever had it, causing destructive clears of locally-set parents never pushed to the peer.

A fail-open read (get_parent_map degradation to {}, truncated page walk) must never overwrite a good peer-parent observation with 'no parent', or the next pass reads a deletion and data loss repeats by a longer route.
On first pass after the fix lands, no binding has a recorded observation so nothing clears; the feature becomes live per-binding as observations accumulate, self-healing into correctness.
